chunks: With this chain of transmission: concerning a man whose forearm, or a place among the places of wudu (ablution), is broken, and he is unable to wipe over it in the state of splinting when it has been set—how should he act? He said:

If he wishes to perform wudu (ablution), then let him place a vessel containing water, and place the site of the splint in the water until the water reaches his skin; that will suffice him without having to undo it.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This is to be understood as a form of recommendation, because we have already explained that with splints it suffices to wipe over them if undoing them is not possible; and if undoing them is possible, then that is necessary. So this is to be understood according to what we said regarding recommendation.
(1355) 28 — Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, who said:

Sulaymān ibn Rushayd wrote to him, informing him that he had urinated in the darkness of the night, and that the coolness of a drop of urine had touched his palm; he had no doubt that it had touched him, though he did not see it. He wiped it with a cloth, then forgot to wash it, and then applied oil and wiped his two palms, his face, and his head with it. Then he performed the wudu (ablution) of salat (prayer) and prayed. So he replied with an answer that I read in his own handwriting:

As for what you merely supposed regarding what touched your hand, it is nothing unless it is something you ascertain. If you did ascertain that, then you would indeed be required to repeat the prayers that you had performed with that very wudu (ablution): those of them whose time still remained, while those whose time had passed, there is no repetition upon you for them. That is because when a man's garment is impure, he does not repeat the salat (prayer) except what remains within its time; but if he is in janabah, or he prayed without wudu (ablution), then he must repeat the prescribed prayers that he missed, because the garment is different from the body. So act upon that, if Allah, the Exalted, wills.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation rather than obligation in legal practice
key_terms.الْبَوْلِ: urine, a source of ritual impurity
key_terms.الْجَبَائِرِ: splints or bandages placed over an injury
key_terms.الْجَبْرِ: the setting or splinting of a broken limb
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification required for salat (prayer)
key_terms.جُنُبًا: in a state of janabah requiring ghusl (ritual bath)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wudu (ablution) with a splint, and must prayers be repeated if urine impurity is only suspected or later confirmed?
ai.summary: This passage addresses rulings of ritual purity, especially concerning splints in wudu (ablution) and the effect of suspected or confirmed najasah on the body during salat (prayer). It distinguishes between mere suspicion and certainty, and between impurity on clothing and invalidity related to the body or absence of wudu (ablution), with different consequences for repeating prayers.
